target.title: fix: detect localized Windows netstat listeners
target.body:
Closes #99984

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on localized Windows installs could run gateway `--force`, port diagnostics, or stale gateway cleanup and have OpenClaw miss an active TCP listener because Windows `netstat` did not print the English `LISTENING` state text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI force-free path, infra diagnostics path, and Windows listening-PID fallback now share one Windows TCP `netstat` listener parser. It matches listener rows by TCP shape, exact local endpoint port, wildcard/port-zero remote endpoint, and positive PID instead of relying on localized state words. The CLI and PID fallback still deduplicate PIDs, while diagnostics keep listener address details.

The QA smoke follow-up keeps the isolated `native-command-session-target` scenario from racing its post-`/stop` recovery turn against the aborted run's session file lock. The scenario now waits for the active session to clear, for the mock delayed provider request to leave `/debug/inflight-requests`, and for the session `.jsonl.lock` file to disappear before it sends the recovery message.

## User Impact

Windows users with non-English system output get more reliable gateway port conflict detection, force-free cleanup, diagnostics, and stale gateway listener verification. Established TCP connections on the target port are not treated as listeners.

The QA smoke scenario now proves native `/stop` unblocks the next turn after the underlying abort cleanup actually finishes, instead of immediately sending recovery traffic while the same session is still locked.

## Evidence

- Head SHA: `fd907fa6ef1c46e21e53fd80a415206b9e5a3d06`
- Claim proved: localized Windows `netstat` listener rows are parsed by the shared CLI, diagnostics, and Windows PID fallback paths without requiring English state text; established/non-wildcard rows on the same port are ignored.
- QA Smoke CI follow-up:
  - Run `28713543047`, job `85150962828`, failed only `Native command active session target evidence`.
  - Scenario report showed `/stop` sent `⚙️ Agent was aborted.`, then the recovery turn received `⚠️ Something went wrong while processing your request. Please try again, or use /new to start a fresh session.`
  - Gateway stderr for that failed scenario showed the recovery turn hit `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError: session file locked (timeout 60000ms)` for the same session lock after `embedded abort settle timed out ... timeoutMs=2000`.
  - Current head updates the scenario to wait for active-run cleanup, mock delayed-provider cleanup, and session lock release before sending the recovery turn.
- Commands / artifacts:
  - `git diff --check`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/program.force.test.ts src/infra/ports.test.ts src/infra/gateway-processes.test.ts`
  - `node --import tsx .artifacts\windows-netstat-proof.ts`
  - `.\node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.cmd --check --threads=1 src/cli/ports.ts src/cli/program.force.test.ts src/infra/ports-inspect.ts src/infra/ports-netstat.ts src/infra/ports.test.ts src/infra/windows-port-pids.ts src/infra/gateway-processes.test.ts`
  - `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_LOCK=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cli/ports.ts src/cli/program.force.test.ts src/infra/ports-inspect.ts src/infra/ports-netstat.ts src/infra/ports.test.ts src/infra/windows-port-pids.ts src/infra/gateway-processes.test.ts`
  - `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-catalog.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-catalog.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-packs.test.ts`
- Observed result:
  - Vitest passed 3 focused netstat files: `src/infra/ports.test.ts` with 17 passed / 6 skipped, `src/cli/program.force.test.ts` with 23 passed, and `src/infra/gateway-processes.test.ts` coverage for the Windows PID fallback using localized `ABHOEREN` rows plus an ignored same-port established row.
  - QA scenario catalog/pack tests passed: 40 tests across `extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-catalog.test.ts` and `extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-packs.test.ts`.
  - Real Windows proof script passed on `win32 10.0.22631` after starting a live `net.Server`, running `C:\Windows\System32\netstat.exe -ano -p tcp`, and parsing the real OS output with this branch's parser:
    - `windows-netstat-proof: PASS`
    - `listenerPort: 55116`
    - `expectedPid: 27296`
    - `realNetstatRow: TCP    127.0.0.1:55116        0.0.0.0:0              LISTENING       27296`
    - `localizedStateRow: TCP    127.0.0.1:55116    0.0.0.0:0    ABHOEREN    27296`
    - `establishedVariantIgnored: TCP    127.0.0.1:55116    127.0.0.1:55117    ESTABLISHED    27296`
  - `git diff --check`, touched-file oxlint, and touched-file oxfmt check passed.
  - Autoreview exited 0 and reported `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`.
  - Current-head `Real behavior proof` passed on run `28714049432`.
- Not tested / proof gaps:
  - This Windows host's native `netstat` output uses English `LISTENING`; I did not have a separate OS-localized Windows install. Localized-state handling is proved by focused fixtures and by replacing the state token on the exact real netstat row captured from this host, then parsing that transformed row through the branch's shared parser.
  - Local focused `qa suite --scenario native-command-session-target` could not run in this Codex worktree because `pnpm openclaw qa suite ...` attempted dependency reconciliation and stopped with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY`, while `node openclaw.mjs qa suite ...` could not run without a built `dist/entry.(m)js`. I avoided broad build/install for this isolated QA YAML repair.
